summary: Hickenlooper called the Gaza ceasefire deal 'a welcome first step towards lasting peace,' urged humanitarian aid for Palestinians and security for Israelis, and repeatedly called for a mutual ceasefire and hostage release.
quote: Palestinians urgently need life-saving aid and Israelis deserve sustained security. All parties must continue down this path to peace and a better future.

summary: Hickenlooper co-signed a letter with 45 Democratic colleagues urging Netanyahu to crack down on West Bank settler violence and investigate deaths of nine American citizens killed by settlers.
quote: We urge you to take measures to prevent and intercede in this violence, establish a credible mechanism to investigate violations of law, and to make clear that the Government of Israel will not tolerate violence by its people

summary: FEC filings show Hickenlooper received $431,868 from pro-Israel PACs, including $325,235 from AIPAC PAC/United Democracy Project, ranking him #34 of 100 senators.
quote: John Hickenlooper has received $431,868 from pro-Israel PACs in FEC filings — $325,235 of it from AIPAC PAC and its super PAC, United Democracy Project

summary: In the 2026 cycle alone, Hickenlooper received $392,685 from pro-Israel PACs (AIPAC $325K, NORPAC $50K, J Street PAC $15K) for his Colorado Senate re-election.
quote: John Hickenlooper has received $392,685 from pro-Israel PACs in the 2026 cycle, chiefly from AIPAC PAC (FEC filings through 2026-10-15).

summary: Hickenlooper posted that he joined Colorado's Jewish community in Boulder to honor victims of a terror attack and 'stand up to antisemitism in all its forms,' framing the moment around antisemitism rather than the Gaza conflict.
quote: Joined Colorado's Jewish community in Boulder today to honor the victims from last week's terror attack and stand up to antisemitism in all its forms.

summary: Hickenlooper voted against two Senate resolutions to partially block military aid to Israel, joining the Republican majority in defeating both measures (73-24, 70-27).
quote: Sens. John Hickenlooper and Michael Bennet were not moved by the increasing alarm over the situation in Gaza, unlike a majority of Democrats who backed both of Sanders' measures.
